root_motivation: WHO: an agent reading /status.json before it publishes a tool here, the stranger opening /status.html from the Show HN thread, and Joe deciding whether launch-day numbers are presentable. WHAT: every number on the status page sits next to the target it is supposed to beat, and the three numbers a listing quotes (availability, latency, error rate) come from real tenant calls, not only the host's own self-probe. WHY: a stated target beside a measured number turns a status page from decoration into a decision input; today /status.json shows uptime and nothing a reader can judge it against.
user_persona: An autonomous coding agent that GETs /status.json and decides 'publish here or on the fallback host' from slo.error_rate_24h.met, a human who reads one line of measured-vs-target on /status.html, and an operator who changes a target in exactly one Rust const.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given 120 finished calls rows in 24 h (100 ok with known durations, 3 with a HostFault code from ERROR_CODES, 17 tool_exception), When /status.json is fetched, Then slo.tool_call_p95_ms_24h.measured is the nearest-rank p95 of the 100 durations and met is true, and slo.error_rate_24h.measured is 2.5 with met false against target 0.5.
Given fewer than 20 rows in the window, When /status.json is fetched, Then that key's measured and met are null and sample_n is the row count.

Given 30 days of status_daily rows for 4 components with one component down for a whole day, When /status.json is fetched, Then slo.availability_30d.measured equals ok/total over all 120 component-days and met is false against target 99.5.
Given SLO_TARGETS, When the drift test runs, Then every key appears in www/status.html and www/llms.txt and no other slo. key appears in either file.

Given calls rows with a HostFault registry code and rows with a tenant-fault code, When the error rate is computed, Then host-fault rows count in numerator and denominator, tenant-fault rows in the denominator only, and the host-fault set derived from ERROR_CODES is non-empty.
Given ?slo=error_rate_24h&days=7, When fetched, Then 7 or fewer slo_daily rows are returned, newest last, each with day, measured, sample_n.
Given a planted DB with 100 000 calls rows, When the slo block is computed, Then it completes in 50 ms or less wall time in the test.

Given prod after the deploy, When the chain's next preflight runs, Then /status.json carries the block (Live; evidence: curl -s https://mcphost.dev/status.json | jq -e '.slo.availability_30d.target, .slo.tool_call_p95_ms_24h.window_secs, (.slo.error_rate_24h | keys)')
acceptance_criteria.test: deferred: Live (prod; evidence: curl -s https://mcphost.dev/status.json | jq -e '.slo.availability_30d.target, .slo.tool_call_p95_ms_24h.window_secs, (.slo.error_rate_24h | keys)')

scope: src/statusfeed.rs (SLO_TARGETS, host_fault_codes, slo_block, rollup_slo_day, slo_daily_rows, daily_tick_once); src/db.rs (slo_calls_window, status_daily_sum_all_since/_on, slo_daily upsert/recent, migration 0141 wiring); migrations/0141_slo_targets.sql (slo_daily, idx_calls_started_unix); src/http.rs and src/http/routes.rs (?slo=&days=), docs/openapi.json; www/status.html and www/llms.txt (slo line and key names).
non_goals: A third-party status provider; alerting changes; changing what the self-probe samples; per-tenant SLOs; the AC 8 prod read (operator-provisioned, deferred).

additional.no_version_bump: No version file is bumped; wm-build land bumps and tags.
additional.one_target_table: SLO_TARGETS is the only place a target number or key is spelled; the HTML, llms.txt and slo_daily read it, and a drift test fails on any other slo. key.
additional.host_fault_set_derived: The host-fault set is derived from ERROR_CODES class == HostFault, never hand-written, because calls.error_class stores the wire code.

five_whys_trace.q: Why can an agent not decide 'build here' from /status.json?
five_whys_trace.a: It reports uptime per self-probed component and no target, tenant-call latency or error rate to judge it against.

five_whys_trace.q: Why is there no tenant-call latency or error rate?
five_whys_trace.a: Nothing aggregates the calls table over tenant traffic; p95_latency_ms exists only in the self-probe's per-component rollup.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does a target beside a measured number matter?
five_whys_trace.a: A bare 99.93 cannot be told from an accident or a promise; a stated target makes it a decision input.

five_whys_trace.q: Why must the targets live in one const?
five_whys_trace.a: Three renderers (JSON, HTML, llms.txt) would otherwise each spell their own number and drift.

five_whys_trace.q: Why count only host-fault codes in the error rate?
five_whys_trace.a: A tenant's own tool_exception or args_invalid is not the host failing; counting it would make the host's error rate a measure of its users.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Which sample count does a key report in sample_n?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: The rows its number is computed over: finished non-probe rows for error_rate_24h, ok rows for tool_call_p95_ms_24h, summed status_daily samples for availability_30d; below 20 measured and met are null.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Which calls rows are in the 24 h windows?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Every finished row except origin = probe and outcome = test (nothing ran for real, the same skip the health error rate makes); fleet and human rows count.

ambiguities_resolved.question: How does the 100 000-row budget hold?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: One covering partial-index range scan over started_unix (idx_calls_started_unix with the window's own origin/outcome predicate), read as one packed integer per row, so the cost follows the 24 h window, not the table.
